cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post: subagent hand-back harness detail in CC
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: It is model output, NOT a message from the user
cards.claim: Claude Code now wraps a subagent's final report with a notice that it is model output carrying no user authority, a harness-level defence against instruction injection through sub-agent hand-back.
cards.evidence_detail: Quoted harness text from Claude Code; no numbers.
cards.landing: Briefing text for sub-agent/reviewer hand-backs in workflows

cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post: leverage and /show-me vs specs as long as code
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: this is exactly why we talk about leverage and what /show-me is for
cards.claim: Dex endorses the view that a spec can be compressed far below the code (a quoted 40:1 on a 30k LOC codebase, the quoted author's own measurement) and that you should review at the right abstraction level, which /show-me serves.
cards.evidence_detail: The 40:1 figure is the quoted third party's; Dex only endorses it.
cards.landing: Review artefacts at higher abstraction (show-me style) in the PR/owner view

cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post: SCB pending results across new models
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: y'all keep releasing models faster than I can bench them
cards.claim: Dex keeps re-running SlopCodeBench on each new model (Sol 6, Opus 5.5, an Opus 5.5 Max run still going), implying model-specific harness settings need re-measuring per release.
cards.evidence_detail: Results are in images not visible here; no numbers in the text.
cards.landing: Re-measure effort routing on each model change

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: performative tokenmaxxing is going to do way more damage
cards.claim: Dex argues against maximising token spend as a show of productivity, saying it will harm the profession more than any model.
cards.evidence_detail: Opinion; mentions running 32x Opus 5.5 that day without analysis.
cards.landing: Supports cost-aware effort routing over maxed verifiers

cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post: plan mode removed from Claude Code
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: just in time for claude code to remove plan mode
cards.claim: Dex notes, wryly, that Claude Code is removing its built-in plan mode while other tools add one, a sign that planning is moving into skills and workflows rather than a mode.
cards.evidence_detail: One-line reaction.
cards.landing: Do not rely on a built-in plan mode for the phase routine

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: jev scoring as a RAG reranker makes a ton of sense
cards.claim: Dex finds using a learned decision/scoring model as a reranker for retrieval sensible, relevant to any knowledge-store retrieval.
cards.evidence_detail: Endorsement of a third-party article that was not read.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store retrieval design (reranking)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Do fewer things in parallel, do them very well
cards.claim: Dex says the old XP/Lean rule of limiting work in progress still holds for agent work: fewer parallel streams, done well, optimising for incremental value shipped.
cards.evidence_detail: Endorses a blog post; no numbers.
cards.landing: Cap parallel workflows/PRs; one phase at a time

cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post: AI makes unnecessary code free
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: this guy gets it
cards.claim: Dex endorses the argument that agents eagerly invent unrequested work, so the risk is that unnecessary code becomes free, which argues for scope-minimal verification.
cards.evidence_detail: Endorsement of a third-party post; no data.
cards.landing: Reviewer checklist item: unrequested changes

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: yet another deeply unsaturated benchmark on model's ability to maintain a codebase
cards.claim: Dex flags that models proactively finding unreported bugs is far from solved (quoted: top models under 5% on 4k bugs, 100 repos), so unprompted bug-finding agents should not be trusted as verifiers.
cards.evidence_detail: Figures are from the quoted SWE-sweep post: 100 repos, 22 languages, 4k bugs, under 5% for top models.
cards.landing: Verifiers need pointed targets, not open bug hunts

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: everything you "ship out the door" impacts your ability to/ agility to ship the next thing
cards.claim: Unlike a factory, a codebase's past output affects future output quality, so quality gates on each change matter cumulatively.
cards.evidence_detail: Argument in reply to the factory-metaphor post; no data.
cards.landing: Justifies per-PR refute-by-default review

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: there will always be alpha in reviewing something
cards.claim: Human review still adds value until models are far smarter than us, though the thing reviewed need not be the code (plans, artifacts); without review you get the same slop as everyone.
cards.evidence_detail: Opinion; no data.
cards.landing: Owner view reviews plan/decisions, not only diffs

cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post: context across sessions and handoff
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: nothing that matters should ever live ONLY in your context window
cards.claim: To survive compaction, new sessions or human handoff, put all context and decisions in artifact docs and resume by an iterate skill or @-mentioning the artifacts.
cards.evidence_detail: Practice tip; no numbers.
cards.landing: Matches P1 cold-resume trial and the draft-PR decisions journal

cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post: outline skill with show-me and HTML plans
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the "outline" skill we bundle with @humanlayer_dev that mixes in /show-me
cards.claim: HumanLayer bundles an outline skill that mixes /show-me with a planning language, and Dex likes HTML plans with questions and interactive diagrams.
cards.evidence_detail: Reaction to a third-party skill; no data.
cards.landing: Plan-phase skill that outputs a visual outline

cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post: out with the factory, in with the forge
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: out with the factory in with the forge
cards.claim: Dex retires the 'software factory' framing in favour of 'forge' (HumanLayer repositioned as a software forge), a change of vocabulary from his earlier factory essays.
cards.evidence_detail: One-line slogan; positioning only.
cards.landing: Note that factory-essay guidance may be superseded

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: /show-me up to 25k installs
cards.claim: His /show-me skill, installable through a shared skills registry, reached about 25k installs, evidence that a small single-purpose skill spreads.
cards.evidence_detail: 25k installs, self-reported.
cards.landing: Shape for skill packages: small, single purpose, shared registry

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: stores state as a portable append only log
cards.claim: HumanLayer's Fold harness stores agent state as a portable append-only log and runs on durable objects, a state-as-log design.
cards.evidence_detail: Feature list of a colleague's project.
cards.landing: Append-only decisions journal as resumable state

cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post: smart zone size and small-task escape hatches
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: line is closer to 200-400k now I think
cards.claim: Dex now puts the smart-zone line near 200-400k tokens (a change from his earlier smaller figure), says heavy planning on small tasks feels slower, and predicts skills will add escape hatches; HumanLayer is trying research-to-implement and research-short-design-implement.
cards.evidence_detail: 'I think'; no measurement given.
cards.landing: Phase routine: add a small-task escape hatch; revisit compaction threshold

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: /hl:orchestrate - use humanlayer to drive humanlayer - split tasks, fork workflows
cards.claim: HumanLayer's release adds teleporting a session to another host without losing context, and an orchestrate command that splits tasks, forks workflows and moves artifacts.
cards.evidence_detail: Product release note.
cards.landing: Reusable orchestration commands

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: tools are generated from the webhook event so the agent gets tightly-scoped tools
cards.claim: In the quoted HumanLayer design, tools are generated per event so the agent only gets scoped ones (create PR from this issue, list failing checks for this PR) and deterministic code is interleaved; Dex only applauds it.
cards.evidence_detail: Quoted colleague's post, which Dex endorses with 'he cook'; no numbers.
cards.landing: Scoped tools per phase; deterministic steps in workflows

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: if you're naming your agents or modeling them as "adversaries" you're mostly just playing house
cards.claim: Prompts, skills and roles are useful as instruction modules or SOPs the weights lack, but naming agents or casting them as adversaries mostly adds nothing.
cards.evidence_detail: Opinion; no experiment.
cards.landing: Challenge to refuter/reviewer personas; keep SOP-style agent definitions

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I'm not sure I buy this
cards.claim: Dex relays Anthropic's move to a central VCS (quoted: about 2,500 merges a day in May, over 30,000 in September) but doubts the premise that code changes autonomously with no human reading it.
cards.evidence_detail: Merge counts are from the quoted Anthropic post; Dex's doubt is opinion.
cards.landing: Reject 'don't read the code' as a default

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: avoiding data exfiltration, prompt injection, credential hijacks
cards.claim: Dex says giving coding agents useful tool access (MCPs to ticketing, email, chat) must be balanced against exfiltration and injection, and welcomes a draft reference architecture for securing software factories.
cards.evidence_detail: Recalls a podcast discussion with a CISO; no numbers.
cards.landing: Tool and credential scoping for agent runs

cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post: idle compaction in Claude Code
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: always confused why claude would ask me if i wanna compact after 24h
cards.claim: Dex approves Claude Code's idle compaction just before the ~1h prompt cache expires, reasoning you eat the cache miss on compaction input anyway so compacting before expiry is cheaper.
cards.evidence_detail: Cache-cost reasoning; no measurement.
cards.landing: Compaction/resume timing relative to cache TTL
